_comment: Canonical percent_left -> displayed number truth table.
Read by BOTH halves of the codebase so the Swift and Python formatters
cannot drift silently:
- app/GradusKit/Tests/GradusKitTests/PercentFormatTests.swift (Swift)
- tests/test_ui.py::PercentFormatTruthTableTest               (Python)
Same placement constraint as signal-levels.json: it lives inside the
SwiftPM test target because SwiftPM resources cannot reference files
outside the target directory. Python reads it by relative path.
`text` is the number ALONE. The '%' suffix and the spoken 'percent
remaining' phrasing are the call site's business, the same way
SignalLevel vends `rgbHex` and lets each app apply its own Color(hex:).
THE THREE RULES THIS TABLE PINS, and why each has a case that fails if
someone 'simplifies' it away:
1. TRUNCATE, never round. percent_left is remaining budget, so rounding
up tells you that you have more than you do. 47.8 -> 47, not 48.
2. ONE DECIMAL BELOW 10. This is correctness, not decoration. The
depleted ceiling is 0.5 (WarningPredicate.depletedPercentCeiling /
snapshot.percent_is_depleted), so a window at 0.6-0.9 is LIVE -- but
integer truncation renders it '0', which reads as exhausted. The
0.5/0.6 pair below is what encodes that boundary. Before 2026-08-06
every Swift call site was `Int(window.percentLeft)` and did exactly
this: displayed a live window, and spoke it aloud to VoiceOver, as 0%.
3. EPSILON-GUARDED FLOOR. percent_left is computed (`100.0 - used`), so
a true 9.1 arrives as 9.099999999999994 and a naive floor drops it to
9.0. Measured over the realistic producer range: 40 such values below
10 and 123 overall. floor(p * m + 1e-9) / m fixes all of them. The two
`_hazard` cases below are real bit patterns, not hand-written decimals;
both languages parse them to the identical IEEE 754 double.

cases.why: LIVE window just over the ceiling -- integer truncation would say '0' and read as exhausted
still live, still truncates to '0' under the old Int() rule
_hazard: true 9.1 as produced by 100.0 - 90.9; a naive floor yields 9.0
truncates DOWN to 9.9; rounding would cross the band into 10.0
_hazard: true 29 as produced by 0.29 * 100; a naive floor yields 28
the case David saw: TUI showed 48, phone showed 47
